A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LDR research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison, including matching content across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and sampling experiments on a Gaussian mixture, alanine dipeptide, and alanine hexapeptide, including numerical results and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results comparing dispersion penalties, loss-weight sensitivity, and training stability.

M1.justification: Section 3 broadens the power-penalty family to general nonnegative penalties rho that vanish only at zero. Appendix D.3 introduces and evaluates a Huber variant. The main L1/L2 procedure, architectures, and Cartesian augmentation correction are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian mixture and molecular systems under unbiased, biased, variational, and Cartesian-coordinate settings. The added analyses use existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 9 adds evaluated comparison variants LDR-L1.5, LDR-L3, and LDR-Huber alongside forward KL and LDR-L1/L2. The existing external comparator sets, including path-gradient forward KL, FAB, and TA-BG, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Added analyses introduce a hexapeptide loss-weight sweep and gradient-norm variance measured in 10,000-step sliding windows. v2 also removes Section 4.4's blanket statement that all methods use equal gradient-step budgets. Existing tabulated settings remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix D substantially expands robustness and mechanism analysis: loss-weight sensitivity now includes hexapeptide, the loss-only failure experiment adds LDR-L2, and a new study compares five dispersion penalties and their gradient variability. The earlier dipeptide sensitivity and reduced-budget CMT analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies that the Welch tests are uncorrected and capture seed-level variability only. Existing run counts, standard-deviation reporting, and significance thresholds are retained; no increase in repetitions is reported.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and the matched Appendix E tables are unchanged. New Table 9 reports ESS of 16.74 ± 0.20% for LDR-L1.5, 8.95 ± 0.26% for LDR-L3, and 16.88 ± 0.40% for LDR-Huber. Additional plots report sensitivity, loss-only failure, and gradient-variability findings.

T1.justification: Appendix A extends Propositions A.1–A.3 and their proofs from power penalties to the broader rho family, explicitly assuming well-defined expectations. Appendix C.1 generalizes the augmented loss accordingly. The existing gradient analysis and augmentation-correction derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same off-policy regularization contribution, application settings, and up-to-tenfold efficiency claim. The revised contribution list highlights L1 robustness already discussed in v1, without materially changing the central scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains that importance resampling cannot recover missing proposal modes and qualifies biased-data costs because initialization uses known modes. It also expands the interpretation of weaker-tail penalties and the relationship between LDR and path-gradient variance reduction.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement replaces promised releases with a stated code repository and dataset-access route. Appendix B.6 newly documents cosine regularization warm-up of 20,000, 50,000, or 100,000 steps, its absence for CMT, and resampling to 10 million samples. These are substantial reproducibility disclosures, without establishing changes to retained runs.

R1.justification: Appendix D.5 adds Vaitl et al. (2022) and expands positioning relative to path-gradient estimators, including their reverse-KL origins and complementary use of target gradients. Most other citation changes update publication metadata rather than introduce different research.

P1.justification: v2 revises the contribution list and method exposition, improves cross-references and terminology, expands appendix discussion, and adds an impact statement. The overall section organization and narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 5 and 7 and Table 9, expands the loss-only visualization with an LDR-L2 panel, and adds color scales to the final density plots. Existing displays are locally reformatted or relocated while the overall layout is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports the stability interpretation through the new penalty and gradient analyses, supplies missing reproduction details, and clarifies statistical and biased-sampling limitations. These improve evidential support and transparency around an already established empirical contribution; the main benchmark results and conclusions remain unchanged.
